title: Why Use GeoSilo?
description: DuckDB's [`spatial` extension](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/spatial) stores geometry as [WKB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Well-known_text_representation_of_geometry) — float64 coordinate pairs at 16 bytes each, even though adjacent vertices in a polygon share nearly all their bits. GeoSilo replaces that with a delta-encoded integer layout and a first-class `GEOSILO` column type. Most existing SQL keeps working because GeoSilo overlays the same `ST_*` surface; the introspection / bounding-box / measurement calls get **native** overloads that skip the WKB decode entirely.

sections.title: What this extension is for
sections.description: Compact geometry storage with a transparent `ST_*` surface. The `GEOSILO` type is a drop-in replacement for `GEOMETRY` columns in the cases GeoSilo targets — large static or slowly-changing polygon / point datasets where on-disk size and bounding-box / area / length speed matter more than complex spatial operations.

bulletPoints.label: Smaller on disk
bulletPoints.description: On the [TIGER/Line 2025](https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/tiger-line-file.html) US Census dataset, `GEOSILO + ZSTD` is **~21% smaller than DuckDB's `GEOMETRY`** column (and ~70% smaller as raw blobs vs WKB). The win comes from delta-encoded int16 deltas compressing exceptionally well under [`ZSTD`](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zstd).

bulletPoints.label: Native ST_* fast paths
bulletPoints.description: [`ST_GeometryType`](#st_geometrytype), [`ST_IsEmpty`](#st_isempty), [`ST_NPoints`](#st_npoints), [`ST_X`](#st_x) / [`ST_Y`](#st_y), [`ST_XMin`](#st_xmin) / [`ST_XMax`](#st_xmax) / [`ST_YMin`](#st_ymin) / [`ST_YMax`](#st_ymax), [`ST_Area`](#st_area), [`ST_Length`](#st_length), [`ST_Perimeter`](#st_perimeter) all have GEOSILO-native implementations. They read the silo header or walk the integer delta stream directly — no GEOS round-trip.

bulletPoints.label: Transparent fallback
bulletPoints.description: Any `ST_*` function without a native GEOSILO overload — [`ST_Buffer`](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/spatial), [`ST_Union`](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/spatial), `ST_AsText`, etc. — still works. The implicit `GEOSILO → GEOMETRY` cast runs [`geosilo_decode`](#geosilo_decode) on demand.

bulletPoints.label: Arrow IPC interchange
bulletPoints.description: GeoSilo registers an [Arrow extension type](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/format/CanonicalExtensions.html) named `queryfarm.geosilo`. Producers tag a binary column with that metadata; the DuckDB consumer auto-decodes silo blobs to `GEOMETRY` on read and re-encodes on write. CRS rides through the metadata so scale stays consistent end-to-end.

sections.title: How the encoding works
sections.description: GeoSilo's encoding is straightforward and verifiable from the README. No ML, no learned codec — just delta encoding plus integer scaling.

bulletPoints.label: Coordinates as scaled integers
bulletPoints.description: Each `(x, y)` pair is multiplied by an integer scale and stored as integers. For [`EPSG:4326`](https://epsg.io/4326) (degrees), the default scale is `1e7` — about 1 cm precision. For projected CRSes like UTM or [`EPSG:3857`](https://epsg.io/3857) (meters), the default is `100`, also 1 cm.

bulletPoints.label: Delta encoding within rings
bulletPoints.description: The first vertex of each ring is stored as a 4-byte int32. Every subsequent vertex is a **2-byte int16 [delta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delta_encoding)** from the previous one. Roughly 90% of deltas fit in 2 bytes; the remainder fall back to a 6-byte escape sequence.

bulletPoints.label: Tight headers, no closing vertex
bulletPoints.description: Points use a 1-byte compact header. Polygon rings omit the closing duplicate vertex (it's reconstructed on decode). The header carries `geometry_type`, `vertex_type`, and `scale`, all readable by [`geosilo_metadata`](#geosilo_metadata) without touching the body.

bulletPoints.label: Bounding-box and area on integers
bulletPoints.description: Native `ST_XMin`/`XMax`/`YMin`/`YMax` walk the int16 delta stream and accumulate; native `ST_Area` runs the [shoelace formula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoelace_formula) on int64 coordinates rebuilt from the same stream. Both avoid the GEOS dependency surface for these calls.

sections.title: Honest scope
sections.description: GeoSilo is a storage and fast-path extension, not a replacement for GEOS-backed spatial operations.

bulletPoints.label: Native overloads are limited
bulletPoints.description: The native fast path covers introspection, bounding-box accessors, and area / length / perimeter. Operations like `ST_Buffer`, `ST_Union`, `ST_Intersection`, `ST_AsText`, and most of the wider `ST_*` surface still auto-decode to `GEOMETRY` and use [`spatial`](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/spatial)'s GEOS-backed implementation.

bulletPoints.label: Lossy at the chosen scale
bulletPoints.description: Coordinates round to the integer scale you pick. The defaults give ~1 cm precision for the common CRSes; finer-grained data needs an explicit `geosilo_encode(geom, scale)`. Round-tripping through GeoSilo and back is **not bit-exact** with the original float64 WKB.

bulletPoints.label: ZSTD does the heavy lifting
bulletPoints.description: Without [`ZSTD`](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zstd), raw GEOSILO blobs are actually larger than DuckDB's columnar `GEOMETRY` storage. `USING COMPRESSION zstd` is what makes the storage win real — use it.

bulletPoints.label: Spatial extension required
bulletPoints.description: GeoSilo overlays [`spatial`](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/spatial)'s `ST_*` namespace. Load `spatial` first, then `geosilo`, in every connection that needs the GEOSILO type.

useCases.title: Shrink a static polygon dataset
useCases.description: TIGER/Line, OSM extracts, parcels, admin boundaries — geometry that's read often and rewritten rarely. Define the column as [`GEOSILO`](#how-the-encoding-works) `USING COMPRESSION zstd` and the same SQL keeps working at a fraction of the storage cost.

useCases.title: Native bounding-box prefilter
useCases.description: Filter on [`ST_XMin`](#st_xmin) / [`ST_XMax`](#st_xmax) / [`ST_YMin`](#st_ymin) / [`ST_YMax`](#st_ymax) before any GEOS-backed operation. The native overloads run on integer deltas — fast enough that the prefilter pays for itself even in single-table scans.

useCases.title: Compact geometry over the wire
useCases.description: Use the [`queryfarm.geosilo`](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/format/CanonicalExtensions.html) Arrow extension type to ship encoded geometry between services. Smaller payloads, transparent decode at the DuckDB consumer.

useCases.title: Fast measurement scans
useCases.description: Per-row [`ST_Area`](#st_area) / [`ST_Length`](#st_length) / [`ST_Perimeter`](#st_perimeter) on millions of polygons without the WKB decode loop. The shoelace runs on int64; `ZSTD` keeps the data small enough that I/O isn't the bottleneck either.
